subject: Statistician position open in the US Forest Service

messages.author: 247b990d236a7af6
messages.subject: Statistician position open in the US Forest Service
parts:
We have an open position for which we are doing outreach prior to announcing the job in USAJobs (USAJobs.gov) sometime in March or early April.

 

The job is a GS-12 Mathematical Statistician and we're looking for someone who is "applied" and has an interest in the natural sciences.  The incumbent would be providing statistical consulting dealing with fire, trees, birds (spotted owls, marbled murrelets, etc.), snow, water, bugs, genetics, and plants, just to name a few topics.  One would certainly be using unmarked.  (I hope that qualifies this as an appropriate post.)

 

The exact job location is still to be determined but will be in California at one of our labs:  Albany, Davis, Riverside, Placerville, Arcata, or Redding.  I've attached the outreach announcement and if you respond by March 4th, I'll make sure you get the USAJobs announcement as soon as it appears.

 

Thanks,

 

Jim

 

Jim Baldwin, Ph. D.

Station Statistician

Forest Service

Pacific Southwest Research Station

p: 510-883-8821

parts:
HI Jim,

I didn't respond by March 4, mostly because I have a GS 12 statistician position with USFWS in Arcata and wouldn't be all that interested in a straight lateral. However, I would be interested if this GS 12 was offered at locations that includes Arcata, and might lead, relatively soon, to the potential for a grade increase, via a related job's opening with the FS or otherwise. I'm on the unmarked google group with my personal email, and not my work email. Perhaps you can't say one way or the other, but I'm potentially interested in the job you floated to the unmarked group.

Nick Som

messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] Statistician position open in the US Forest Service
parts:
I'm hopeful that the job will be on USAJobs.gov within a couple of weeks.  In any event, when it becomes available, I'll include you on the mailing list.

As you probably know promotions "in place" are becoming very rare (at least in the Forest Service).  Almost all increases in GS level occur when a new or vacant job is advertised.  In other words, all promotions involve competition.  (The exception is a paneled scientist where promotions are determined by research quality:  publications, technology transfer, etc.)  This job will likely stay at a GS-12 for quite some time.  A GS-13 or GS-14 statistician position might open up when I retire (which is looking sooner and sooner - the retirement that is.)

Jim
